Subject: Architecture review — scheduling and pre-read

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for agreeing to an architecture deep-dive on Redwood's serving/runtime for the Acme integration. We proposed Jul 15 (Thu) 11:00am PT on the invite but wanted to confirm that still works for you and your platform team.

High level goal: walk through the proposed runtime topology, KV cache / batching behavior for your workload profile, and integration points for telemetry and security (KMS/HSM). We expect this to run ~60–75 minutes (40 minutes presentation + 20–35 minutes Q/A deep dive).

Initial asks:
- Can you share a short list of attendees and any specific topics you want emphasized (e.g., latency SLOs, isolation, encryption-at-rest)?
- We'll circulate a short pre-read (slides + diagrams) 48 hours before the meeting — are there any docs on your side we should review?

I've looped in Marissa (runtime lead) and Jonas (infra/product) from our side. If Jul 15 doesn't work, happy to propose alternatives.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop

Looping in a couple of technical notes for the pre-read and agenda. Please see comments inline below and in the attached diagram stub.

On the pre-read:
- I'll add a slide that shows expected token/sequence length distribution for Acme's workload (this will help justify batching/kv cache sizing).
- Recommend including the quantization profile options we plan to offer (int8 vs int4 tradeoffs) and the expected latency delta per profile.
- For the system diagram, please include: 1) routing policy fallbacks (hosted -> dedicated -> private variants), 2) KV cache placement (edge vs serving), and 3) telemetry hooks (trace id propagation example).

Agenda suggestions (tight 60–75m):
- 0–5m: intros and goals
- 5–25m: runtime topology + data flow (Marissa)
- 25–45m: integration points and security (Jonas)
- 45–65m: Q/A and open issues (all)
- 65–75m: follow-ups & mutual action items

I'll attach a png of the draft topology for Lauren to include in the pre-read.
